title: How to Choose CAS Activities That Won't Feel Like…
summary: Choose meaningful IB CAS activities for September to November using practical checks for interest, sustainability, personal growth, evidence, and impact.
body_markdown:
Choosing CAS activities that will not feel like a chore starts with a simple principle: select experiences connected to interests, routines, people, or causes already important to you. Then check that each idea offers genuine challenge, visible learning, manageable logistics, and a clear connection to **Creativity, Activity, or Service** .


This is particularly important from September to November. An exciting idea chosen in September can become an obligation by October if it requires difficult travel, constant coordination, or more time than your academic schedule allows. The aim is not to avoid effort, but to choose effort that feels worthwhile and remains sustainable.


### Understand what CAS requires


CAS is a compulsory part of the IB Diploma Programme core, although it is **not formally graded** . The[official IB overview of CAS](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/creativity-activity-and-service/) defines three strands:


- **Creativity:** exploring and extending ideas to produce an original or interpretive product or performance
- **Activity:** physical exertion contributing to a healthy lifestyle
- **Service:** collaborative and reciprocal engagement with a community in response to an authentic need


The IB framework expects CAS to continue regularly for **at least 18 months** , with reasonable balance among the strands. Students maintain a portfolio, reflect purposefully, and provide evidence that they have achieved all **seven CAS learning outcomes** . The[official CAS subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/cas-2016-english-1st-final-web.pdf) summarizes these expectations.


You must also complete at least one **CAS project** , meaning a collaborative series of planned experiences lasting at least one month. It may address one, two, or all three strands. The[IB CAS project guidance](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/creativity-activity-and-service/cas-projects/) emphasizes initiative, perseverance, collaboration, problem-solving, and decision-making.


The IB does not prescribe a universal list of acceptable activities or a current universal hours target. Schools may set approval procedures, deadlines, safety rules, or participation expectations, so consult your CAS coordinator. RevisionDojo's[guide to minimum CAS requirements](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/understanding-the-minimum-requirements-for-cas-in-the-ibdp) helps distinguish the IB framework from school-specific rules.


### Use the motivation, meaning, and maintenance test


Assess each idea in three areas before committing.


Test Question to ask Warning sign


Motivation Would part of this interest me without CAS? You only want a portfolio entry


Meaning Will someone learn, grow, create, or benefit? The purpose is artificial or vague


Maintenance Can I continue during busy academic weeks? It depends on an unusually quiet schedule


A suitable experience need not be your greatest passion. It should contain at least one source of motivation, such as friendship, curiosity, movement, responsibility, creative control, or connection to a cause.


Maintenance matters equally. Nearby weekly tutoring may be more sustainable than occasional volunteering requiring two hours of travel. A straightforward activity you continue is generally more valuable than an impressive proposal you abandon.


### Build from your existing interests


List what you already do, enjoy, or want to improve. This reduces the difficulty of creating an entirely new routine.


- If you draw, design materials for a community organization.
- If you enjoy running, establish a progressive training goal or organize a small group.
- If you are confident in a subject, tutor younger students through structured lessons.
- If you enjoy music, learn a new style or help younger musicians rehearse.
- If you care about waste, investigate a local need before planning an initiative.


An existing hobby does not automatically become CAS because you record it. Add **intention, challenge, goals, reflection, and evidence** . Casual jogging, for example, becomes more purposeful when you establish a safe progression goal, monitor consistency, and reflect on setbacks. The[RevisionDojo guide to jogging as CAS](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/can-jogging-be-considered-a-cas-experience) explains this distinction.


CAS also cannot duplicate work submitted for a DP subject. Ask your coordinator if an experience might overlap with coursework.


### Choose a realistic fall-term combination


Avoid launching several demanding commitments simultaneously. Select a small number of dependable **anchor experiences** , then leave room for shorter opportunities.


Period Main task Example


September Explore and test Attend clubs, contact a partner, or test a fitness routine


October Establish consistency Continue a weekly experience and collect evidence


November Review and adjust Evaluate workload, learning, enjoyment, and next steps


A possible combination is weekly basketball for Activity, fortnightly tutoring for Service, and occasional design work for Creativity. This is not an official formula, and equal time in each strand is not required. Your overall programme needs a **reasonable balance** , not three identical weekly schedules.


When possible, try an activity two or three times before making a long commitment. Ask whether the challenge is appropriate, the logistics work, and the experience produces meaningful moments for reflection.


### Check practicality and ethical impact


Before agreeing, confirm the schedule, travel time, preparation, supervision, safety procedures, and evidence requirements. Consider what happens during examinations, holidays, illness, or bad weather. Obtain coordinator approval before making a major commitment.


For Service, begin with the community's **authentic need** , not an activity you have already decided to provide. Reciprocal service requires listening and working with people rather than treating them as passive recipients. Consent, dignity, privacy, representation, and long-term usefulness are essential considerations.


Meaningful CAS can still be challenging. Aim for a familiar foundation plus one unfamiliar element, such as learning a new musical style, leading beginner sports sessions, or adapting tutoring explanations for different learners. IB research on the[impact of CAS](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/cas-snapshot-2017-en.pdf) identifies meaningfulness, enjoyment, and goal setting as features associated with successful implementation.


### Make reflection manageable


Record brief notes and evidence soon after significant sessions rather than allowing reflections to accumulate. Focus on what happened, what was difficult, what decision you made, what changed, and what you will do next.


Not every session requires a long essay, and the IB does not prescribe a universal reflection count or word limit. Follow your school's instructions while prioritizing specific evidence of development over repetitive description. RevisionDojo offers practical[CAS reflection guidance](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/10-powerful-tips-to-write-a-cas-reflection-that-stands-out-in-2025) and advice on[balancing CAS with academics](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-balance-cas-with-academics-and-social-life) .


### Common mistakes when choosing CAS activities


- **Starting too many activities:** early enthusiasm can conceal the weekly workload.
- **Choosing by appearance:** an impressive title does not guarantee meaningful growth.
- **Ignoring logistics:** travel and administration often create avoidable frustration.
- **Treating routine participation as sufficient:** CAS requires purposeful goals and reflection.
- **Forcing every outcome into one experience:** outcomes should emerge credibly across the programme.
- **Planning service without consultation:** this may waste resources or undermine participants.
- **Assuming automatic approval:** your school determines whether the experience is acceptable.


### Conclusion


To choose CAS activities that will not feel like a chore, prioritize genuine interest, meaningful purpose, sustainable logistics, and manageable challenge. Test possibilities in September, establish consistency in October, and review your commitments in November.


Keep the programme small enough to sustain but rich enough to produce genuine learning. RevisionDojo's[CAS project and experience comparison](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-counts-as-a-cas-project-vs-a-cas-experience) can help classify your plans, while Jojo AI and CAS reflection resources can support organization without replacing your judgment or voice.
